title: Singapore’s Wong Warns AI Tech Rally Faces Eventual Correction
key_facts: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, also finance minister, spoke at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
He said: 'No boom is forever. At some point, there will be a correction.' and that nobody knows when, how or who the casualties will be.
Singapore's approach is to use the window of external demand to build new capabilities and better jobs.
The AI boom has helped Singapore's chip industry, with firms such as GlobalFoundries and Micron making memory and specialty chips.
He said no country can handle rogue AI alone; international safeguards are ideal, 'perhaps under the auspices of the United Nations', but will take time.
He said safety requirements will vary by sector and cited new Monetary Authority of Singapore guidelines on AI in finance and a Waymo driverless-car pilot.
quote_evidence: “No boom is forever. At some point, there will be a correction. And we don't know when it will happen, or how it will happen, we don't know who the casualties will be when it happens,” said Mr Wong, who is also finance minister.
“It cannot be just confined to a single country, so ideally international safeguards are put in place, perhaps under the auspices of the United Nations. But that will take time,” he said.
Turning to AI’s impact on workers and the jobs market, Mr Wong said Singapore’s approach is “not to protect the job, but to protect every worker”.
why_it_matters_hint: A head of government who is also finance minister warns that the AI boom will correct, while using it to build local capabilities.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; read CNA's own report of the same remarks. Forbes also reported the conference.
